\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The tree}
A \emph{Pythagorean triple} is a triple $(a,b,c)$ of positive integers with
$a^2+b^2=c^2$; it is \emph{primitive} if $\gcd(a,b)=1$. Barning (1963) and Hall (1970),
following Berggren (1934), observed that the primitive triples with odd first leg form a
rooted infinite ternary tree under the action of three explicit integer matrices:
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&-2&2\\2&-1&2\\2&-2&3\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&2\\2&1&2\\2&2&3\end{pmatrix},\qquad
C=\begin{pmatrix}-1&2&2\\-2&1&2\\-2&2&3\end{pmatrix},
\]
with root $\bfr=(3,4,5)^{\mathsf T}$. Explicitly,
\[
\begin{aligned}
A(a,b,c) &= (a-2b+2c,\ 2a-b+2c,\ 2a-2b+3c),\\
B(a,b,c) &= (a+2b+2c,\ 2a+b+2c,\ 2a+2b+3c),\\
C(a,b,c) &= (-a+2b+2c,\ -2a+b+2c,\ -2a+2b+3c),
\end{aligned}
\]
so that $A\bfr=(5,12,13)$, $B\bfr=(21,20,29)$, $C\bfr=(15,8,17)$.

\subsection{The plot, and the phenomenon}
For a triple $v=(a,b,c)$ with $c>0$ put
\[
\dirp(v)=\bigl(x(v),y(v)\bigr):=\Bigl(\frac ac,\frac bc\Bigr),
\]
a point of the unit circle. Draw $v$ inside the closed unit disc at
$\mathrm{draw}(v)=\rho(v)\,\dirp(v)$ with $\rho(v)=1-1/c$, and join each node to its three
children. Two visual features appear:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.7em]
  \item \emph{radiating streaks}, resembling geodesics of the Klein disc;
  \item \emph{stars}: at isolated boundary points, bundles of many curves converging into
        that single point, meeting the circle tangentially rather than transversally.
\end{itemize}
This paper explains both, exactly.

\subsection{Method}
The Pythagorean equation is the vanishing of the quadratic form $Q(a,b,c)=a^2+b^2-c^2$ of
signature $(2,1)$, with polarization $\ip{v}{w}=v_1w_1+v_2w_2-v_3w_3$. All three
generators preserve $\ip{\cdot}{\cdot}$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:lorentz}), hence lie in
$O(2,1;\Z)$. The positive light cone modulo scaling is the boundary circle
$\partial\Hyp^2$ in the Klein model, and $\dirp$ is precisely the ideal-point map. The
plot is therefore a picture of a discrete subgroup of $\Isom(\Hyp^2)$ acting on the circle
at infinity, and the classification of the visible curves is the classification of the
generators by conjugacy type.

\section{The Lorentzian skeleton}

\begin{proposition}[Lorentz invariance]\label{prop:lorentz}
For all $v,w\in\Z^3$ and $M\in\{A,B,C\}$ we have $\ip{Mv}{Mw}=\ip{v}{w}$. In particular
$Q(Mv)=Q(v)$, each generator maps the light cone to itself, and every word in the
generators sends Pythagorean triples to Pythagorean triples.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Expand both sides as polynomials in the six coordinates; each is an identity of quadratic
forms verified by direct expansion.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}
Call $v=(a,b,c)$ \emph{admissible} if $Q(v)=0$, $a\ge0$, $b\ge0$, $c>0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:adm}
On the light cone with nonnegative legs, $a\le c$ and $b\le c$. Each generator maps
admissible vectors to admissible vectors and never decreases the hypotenuse.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
From $a^2+b^2=c^2$ and $b\ge0$ we get $a^2\le c^2$, hence $a\le c$; symmetrically $b\le
c$. The positivity and monotonicity claims are then linear consequences; e.g.\ the first
coordinate of $Cv$ is $-a+2b+2c\ge -c+2b+2c>0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Charge]
For a null vector $p$ with $c_p>0$ and any $v$, the \emph{charge of $v$ at $p$} is
$d=-\ip{v}{p}$.
\end{definition}

Two null lattice vectors are distinguished: $e_1=(1,0,1)$ and $e_2=(0,1,1)$, with
$\dirp(e_1)=(1,0)$ and $\dirp(e_2)=(0,1)$. One computes $\ip{v}{e_1}=a-c$ and
$\ip{v}{e_2}=b-c$, so the corresponding charges are $c-a$ and $c-b$.

\begin{proposition}[Conserved charges]\label{prop:charges}
For every $v=(a,b,c)$,
\[
(Cv)_3-(Cv)_1=c-a,\qquad (Av)_3-(Av)_2=c-b,\qquad (Bv)_1-(Bv)_2=-(a-b).
\]
Thus $C$ fixes the charge at $e_1$ and fixes $e_1$ itself, $A$ fixes the charge at $e_2$
and fixes $e_2$, and $B$ preserves $|a-b|$, whose vanishing locus on the cone is the
direction $(1,1,\sqrt2)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:chargepos}
If $(a,b,c)$ lies on the cone with $b,c>0$, then $c-a>0$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$b^2=(c-a)(c+a)>0$ and $c+a\ge0$ since $|a|\le c$; the case $c=a$ would force $b=0$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Conjugacy types: exact closed forms}

\begin{theorem}[The parabolic flows]\label{thm:parabolic}
Let $d=c-a$ and $e=c-b$. For every $k\ge0$,
\[
C^k(a,b,c)=\bigl(\gamma_k-d,\ b+2kd,\ \gamma_k\bigr),\qquad \gamma_k=c+2kb+2k^2d,
\]
\[
A^k(a,b,c)=\bigl(a+2ke,\ \alpha_k-e,\ \alpha_k\bigr),\qquad \alpha_k=c+2ka+2k^2e .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Induction on $k$; the inductive step is a polynomial identity in $k$ after substituting
the closed form and applying the generator.
\end{proof}

The hypotenuse along either flow is a genuine quadratic polynomial in the step number,
with leading coefficient twice the conserved charge. Quadratic growth of iterates is the
signature of a rank-three unipotent Jordan block, so $A$ and $C$ are \emph{parabolic}
isometries. From the root,
\[
A^k\bfr=\bigl(2k+3,\ 2(k+1)(k+2),\ 2(k+1)(k+2)+1\bigr),\qquad
C^k\bfr=\bigl((2k+1)(2k+3),\ 4k+4,\ (2k+2)^2+1\bigr),
\]
the classical ``legs differ from the hypotenuse by $1$'' and ``by $2$'' families.

\begin{theorem}[The hyperbolic flow]\label{thm:hyperbolic}
For every $v$, $(B^2v)_3=6(Bv)_3-v_3$: the hypotenuse satisfies the Pell recursion
$c_{k+2}=6c_{k+1}-c_k$, whose characteristic roots are the units
$3\pm2\sqrt2=(1\pm\sqrt2)^2$ of $\Z[\sqrt2]$. If $(a,b,c)$ is admissible with $a,b>0$
then $c_{k+1}\ge5c_k$, hence $c_k\ge5^kc_0$. Moreover
$(B^kv)_1-(B^kv)_2=(-1)^k(a-b)$, so $|a-b|$ is constant along the flow.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The recursion is a pointwise polynomial identity, valid because the $(-1)$-eigenvector
$(1,-1,0)$ of $B$ has vanishing third coordinate. For the growth: on the cone with
$a,b>0$ we have $(a+b)^2=c^2+2ab\ge c^2$, so $a+b\ge c$, whence $(Bv)_3=2a+2b+3c\ge5c$.
The charge identity is Proposition~\ref{prop:charges} iterated.
\end{proof}

Thus $B$ is \emph{hyperbolic}: its orbits translate along an axis geodesic, converging
exponentially to the ideal point at angle $\pi/4$, where $a=b$.

\section{The chord--charge identity and the star theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Chord $=$ charge]\label{thm:chord}
Let $v,p$ be null vectors with $c_v,c_p>0$. Then
\[
\bigl\|\dirp v-\dirp p\bigr\|^2=\frac{-2\ip{v}{p}}{c_v\,c_p}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $v=(a,b,c)$, $p=(x,y,z)$. Then
\[
\Bigl(\tfrac ac-\tfrac xz\Bigr)^2+\Bigl(\tfrac bc-\tfrac yz\Bigr)^2
=\frac{a^2+b^2}{c^2}+\frac{x^2+y^2}{z^2}-\frac{2(ax+by)}{cz}
=2-\frac{2(ax+by)}{cz},
\]
using $a^2+b^2=c^2$ and $x^2+y^2=z^2$. Since $\ip{v}{p}=ax+by-cz$, the right-hand side is
$2-2(\ip{v}{p}+cz)/(cz)=-2\ip{v}{p}/(cz)$.
\end{proof}

Every subsequent result is a consequence of Theorem~\ref{thm:chord}.

\begin{definition}[Horocycle of charge $d$]
For null $p$ and $d\in\Z_{>0}$, the set $\{v \text{ on the cone}:\ \ip{v}{p}=-d\}$ is the
level set of a linear functional; in the Klein model it is a \emph{horocycle} based at the
ideal point $\dirp p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Star theorem: horocyclic convergence]\label{thm:star}
Let $p$ be null with $c_p>0$ and let $(w_k)$ be null vectors with $c_{w_k}>0$ satisfying
$\ip{w_k}{p}=-d$ for all $k$ and $c_{w_k}\to\infty$. Then $\dirp(w_k)\to\dirp(p)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:chord}, $\|\dirp w_k-\dirp p\|^2=2d/(c_{w_k}c_p)\to0$; each coordinate
difference is bounded by the square root of this quantity.
\end{proof}

Distinct $d$ give disjoint families, all converging to the same boundary point. That is
\emph{the star}.

\begin{theorem}[Exact tangency]\label{thm:tangency}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:chord},
\[
c_v\cdot\bigl\|\dirp v-\dirp p\bigr\|^2=\frac{-2\ip{v}{p}}{c_p}.
\]
Along a horocycle of charge $d$ based at $p$ this product is therefore \emph{constant},
equal to $2d/c_p$ --- not merely convergent.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Contact order exactly two]\label{cor:contact}
Along a horocycle of charge $d>0$ with $c_{w_k}\to\infty$,
\[
c_{w_k}^2\,\|\dirp w_k-\dirp p\|^2\longrightarrow\infty,
\qquad
\sqrt{c_{w_k}}\,\|\dirp w_k-\dirp p\|^2\longrightarrow0 .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The two expressions equal $c_{w_k}\cdot(2d/c_p)$ and $(2d/c_p)/\sqrt{c_{w_k}}$.
\end{proof}

A geodesic through the centre of the Klein disc meets $\partial\Hyp^2$ transversally
(contact order one). Corollary~\ref{cor:contact} says the star curves have contact order
exactly two --- the visible reason they bend into the rim rather than striking it.

\begin{theorem}[Equation of a drawn spoke]\label{thm:drawn}
If $\ip{v}{p}=-d$ and $r=\rho(v)=1-1/c_v$, then
\[
\bigl\|\dirp v-\dirp p\bigr\|^2=\frac{2d\,(1-r)}{c_p}.
\]
Each spoke is thus the graph of an exact algebraic relation between angular offset and
radial defect, with the single parameter $d/c_p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Drawn convergence]
If $(w_j)$ are admissible of constant charge $d$ at an admissible $p$ with
$c_{w_j}\to\infty$, then $\rho(w_j)\to1$ and $\mathrm{draw}(w_j)\to\dirp(p)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Chord ratio]\label{thm:ratio}
If $v,v'$ are null with $c_v=c_{v'}>0$ and charges $d,d'\ne0$ at $p$, then
\[
\frac{\|\dirp v-\dirp p\|^2}{\|\dirp v'-\dirp p\|^2}=\frac{d}{d'} .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:chord} to both and divide; the common factor $2/(c_vc_p)$ cancels.
\end{proof}

Distinct charges are therefore visibly distinct curves, not a bookkeeping artefact.

\section{Which spokes exist: charge quantization}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:notbothodd}
No Pythagorean triple has both legs odd.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
If $a=2k+1$ and $b=2l+1$ then $a^2+b^2\equiv2\pmod4$, while every square is $0$ or $1$
modulo $4$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:coprime}
In a primitive triple, $\gcd(a,c)=1$ and $c$ is odd.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
If $\gcd(a,b)=1$ then $a$ is coprime to $b^2=c^2-a^2$, hence to $c^2$, hence to $c$. The
legs cannot both be even (primitivity) nor both odd (Lemma~\ref{lem:notbothodd}), so
exactly one is odd and $c^2$ is odd.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Charge quantization]\label{thm:quant}
Let $a^2+b^2=c^2$ with $a,b,c>0$ and $\gcd(a,b)=1$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em]
  \item If $a$ is odd, then $c-a=2n^2$ for some integer $n\ge1$.
  \item If $a$ is even, then $c-a=n^2$ for some \emph{odd} integer $n\ge1$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Suppose $a$ is odd. By Lemma~\ref{lem:notbothodd}, $b=2b'$ is even, and by
Lemma~\ref{lem:coprime} $c$ is odd; so $c-a=2u$ and $c+a=2v$ with $u>0$ by
Proposition~\ref{prop:chargepos}. From $b^2=(c-a)(c+a)$ we get $uv=b'^2$. Writing $c=u+v$
and $a=v-u$ and using $\gcd(a,c)=1$, a B\'ezout combination gives $\gcd(u,v)=1$. Coprime
integers with square product are (up to sign) squares; positivity gives $u=n^2$, so
$c-a=2n^2$.

Suppose $a$ is even. Then $b$ and $c$ are odd, and $c-a$, $c+a$ are odd with product
$b^2$; their gcd divides $2\gcd(a,c)=2$ and both are odd, so they are coprime. Hence
$c-a=n^2$, and $n$ is odd because $c-a$ is odd.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Realisability]\label{thm:realise}
For every $n\ge1$ the triple $(2n+1,\,2n^2+2n,\,2n^2+2n+1)$ is primitive with odd first
leg and charge $c-a=2n^2$; for every $m\ge1$ the triple $(4m,\,4m^2-1,\,4m^2+1)$ is
primitive with even first leg and charge $c-a=(2m-1)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Direct verification, with the explicit B\'ezout relations
$(2n+1)(2n+1)+(2n^2+2n)(-2)=1$ and $(4m)m+(4m^2-1)(-1)=1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Spectrum of the star]\label{cor:spectrum}
A positive integer $d$ is the charge at $(1,0)$ of some primitive Pythagorean triple with
positive entries if and only if $d=2n^2$ for some $n\ge1$, or $d=n^2$ for some odd
$n\ge1$. Restricting to odd first leg --- i.e.\ to nodes of the Berggren tree --- the
spectrum is exactly $\{2n^2:n\ge1\}$.
\end{corollary}

Both sets have density zero in $\Z$. This is the arithmetic reason the star has discrete,
separated spokes.

\section{Euclid coordinates and the spoke index}

\begin{definition}
For $m,n\in\Z$ put $\eu(m,n)=(m^2-n^2,\ 2mn,\ m^2+n^2)$.
\end{definition}

Then $Q(\eu(m,n))=0$ identically, $\eu$ is injective on $0<n<m$, and $\bfr=\eu(2,1)$.

\begin{theorem}[Generators in Euclid coordinates]\label{thm:eu}
\[
A\,\eu(m,n)=\eu(2m-n,\ m),\qquad
B\,\eu(m,n)=\eu(2m+n,\ m),\qquad
C\,\eu(m,n)=\eu(m+2n,\ n).
\]
\end{theorem}

This is the classical ternary tree on coprime parameter pairs. Note the distinction: $C$
\emph{freezes} the smaller parameter $n$, while $A$ and $B$ \emph{promote} $m$ to be the
new smaller parameter.

\begin{theorem}[Charges in Euclid coordinates]\label{thm:euch}
$\ip{\eu(m,n)}{e_1}=-2n^2$ and $\ip{\eu(m,n)}{e_2}=-(m-n)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$a-c=(m^2-n^2)-(m^2+n^2)=-2n^2$ and $b-c=2mn-m^2-n^2=-(m-n)^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Spoke index]
The \emph{spoke index} of a node $\eu(m,n)$ with $0<n<m$ is $n$: the unique integer with
charge $2n^2$ at $(1,0)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Depth bound]\label{thm:depth}
Let $W$ be a word of length $\ell$ in $\{A,B,C\}$ with $W\bfr=\eu(m,n)$, $0<n<m$. Then
$n<2\cdot3^{\ell}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:eu}, one step maps a pair $(m,n)$ with $0<n<m$ to a pair whose larger
parameter is at most $2m+n<3m$, the smaller parameter being at most the previous larger
one. Induction from $\eu(2,1)$ gives larger parameter $\le 2\cdot3^{\ell}$, and the
smaller is strictly less.
\end{proof}

Consequently the $n$-th spoke cannot be drawn before depth roughly $\log_3(n/2)$: the star
fills in at most logarithmically fast. The bound is sharp up to the constant.

\begin{theorem}[Sharpness along the hyperbolic branch]\label{thm:pell}
Let $P_0=1$, $P_1=2$, $P_{k+2}=2P_{k+1}+P_k$ be the Pell numbers. Then
$B^k\bfr=\eu(P_{k+1},P_k)$ and, for $k\ge1$,
\[
2^k\le P_k<2\cdot3^k,\qquad \ip{B^k\bfr}{e_1}=-2P_k^2 .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$\bfr=\eu(P_1,P_0)$ and, by Theorem~\ref{thm:eu},
$B\,\eu(P_{k+1},P_k)=\eu(2P_{k+1}+P_k,P_{k+1})=\eu(P_{k+2},P_{k+1})$. The lower bound
follows by induction from $P_{k+2}=2P_{k+1}+P_k\ge2\cdot2^{k+1}$, the upper bound from
Theorem~\ref{thm:depth}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Slowest growth along the parabolic branch]\label{thm:abranch}
$A^k\bfr=\eu(k+2,\ k+1)$, so the spoke index along the $A$-branch is $k+1$, reaching
spoke $n$ only at depth $n-1$.
\end{theorem}

Theorems~\ref{thm:pell} and \ref{thm:abranch} show that the appealing universal law
``spoke index $n$ appears at depth $\Theta(\log n)$'' is \emph{false}; the correct
universal statement is Theorem~\ref{thm:depth} together with the attaining family of
Theorem~\ref{thm:pell}.

\begin{remark}\label{rem:cfrozen}
Along $C$ the spoke index is frozen: $C^k\eu(m,n)=\eu(m+2kn,\ n)$, so the whole $C$-orbit
of a node lies on a single spoke with the same charge $2n^2$. This makes the $C$-orbit the
natural parametrisation of an individual spoke.
\end{remark}

\section{Escape rates: geodesic versus horocycle}

\begin{lemma}[A sharp circle estimate]\label{lem:circle}
If $x,y\ge0$ and $x^2+y^2=1$, then $\bigl|x-\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\bigr|\le|x-y|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
First $(x+y)^2=1+2xy\le2(x^2+y^2)=2$, so $x+y\le\sqrt2$. Since $2x^2-1=x^2-y^2$,
\[
\Bigl|x-\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\Bigr|\Bigl(x+\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\Bigr)
=\Bigl|x^2-\tfrac12\Bigr|=\tfrac12|x^2-y^2|=\tfrac12|x-y|(x+y)
\le\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}|x-y|\le|x-y|\Bigl(x+\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\Bigr).
\]
Divide by $x+\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}>0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:diag}
For an admissible triple $(a,b,c)$, $\bigl|x(v)-\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\bigr|\le|a-b|/c$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Exponential escape]\label{thm:exp}
For admissible $(a,b,c)$ with $a,b>0$ and all $k\ge0$,
\[
\Bigl|x\bigl(B^k(a,b,c)\bigr)-\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\Bigr|\le\frac{|a-b|}{3^k\,c}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:hyperbolic} the numerator is constant and $c_k\ge3^kc$; apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:diag}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial escape, and no faster]\label{thm:poly}
For admissible $(a,b,c)$ with $b,c>0$ and $k\ge1$,
\[
1-x\bigl(C^k(a,b,c)\bigr)\ \ge\ \frac{c-a}{\bigl(c+2b+2(c-a)\bigr)k^2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:parabolic}, $1-x(C^kv)=(c-a)/\gamma_k$ with
$\gamma_k=c+2kb+2k^2(c-a)\le k^2\bigl(c+2b+2(c-a)\bigr)$ for $k\ge1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Rate dichotomy at the root]\label{cor:dichotomy}
For every $k\ge1$,
\[
\frac{2}{17k^2}\ \le\ 1-x\bigl(C^k\bfr\bigr),
\qquad
\Bigl|x\bigl(B^k\bfr\bigr)-\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\Bigr|\ \le\ \frac{1}{5\cdot3^{k}} .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[No star at the hyperbolic limit]\label{thm:irr}
For every $v$ with $c_v\ne0$, $x(v)\ne\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$x(v)$ is rational and $\sqrt2/2$ is irrational.
\end{proof}

So the ideal point at angle $\pi/4$ is a limit of the plot but never a plotted point:
\emph{stars occur only at rational ideal points}.

\begin{theorem}[Density of star centres]\label{thm:dense}
For every $t\in[0,1)$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there are integers $0<n<m$ with
$\bigl|\frac{m^2-n^2}{m^2+n^2}-t\bigr|<\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The map $g(r)=(r^2-1)/(r^2+1)$ is a continuous increasing bijection $[1,\infty)\to[0,1)$;
put $r_0=\sqrt{(1+t)/(1-t)}$, so $g(r_0)=t$. Rationals $m/n$ with $0<n<m$ are dense in
$(1,\infty)$; choose one in a neighbourhood of $r_0$ on which $g$ varies by less than
$\varepsilon$, and note $g(m/n)=(m^2-n^2)/(m^2+n^2)$.
\end{proof}

\section{Star location and multiplicity}

Words in the generators are Lorentz isometries: $\ip{Wv}{Wp}=\ip{v}{p}$. The key
computation is
\[
A\,e_1=B\,e_1=(3,4,5)=\bfr,\qquad C\,e_1=e_1,
\]
so the orbit of the ideal point $(1,0)$ under the monoid is $\{(1,0)\}$ together with the
ideal points of all tree nodes.

\begin{theorem}[A star at every node]\label{thm:starnode}
For every word $W$ in the generators, the family $j\mapsto W\!A\,C^j\bfr$ consists of
nodes of the tree whose plotted points converge to $\dirp(W\bfr)$. In particular
$\dirp(A\,C^j\bfr)\to(3/5,4/5)$: the root is a star centre.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By the $C$-invariance of the charge at $e_1$ and $\ip{\bfr}{e_1}=3-5=-2$, we have
$\ip{C^j\bfr}{e_1}=-2$ for all $j$. Applying the isometry $W\!A$ preserves the pairing, so
$\ip{W\!AC^j\bfr}{W\!Ae_1}=-2$, and $W\!Ae_1=W\bfr$. Admissibility is preserved
(Proposition~\ref{prop:adm}); the hypotenuse of $C^j\bfr$ exceeds $j$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:parabolic}) and words do not decrease it. Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:star}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Barning--Hall completeness]\label{thm:complete}
Every primitive Pythagorean triple $(a,b,c)$ with $a,b,c>0$ and $a$ odd equals $W\bfr$ for
some word $W$ in $\{A,B,C\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Each generator has an explicit integral inverse:
\[
\begin{aligned}
A^{-1}(a,b,c)&=(a+2b-2c,\ -2a-b+2c,\ -2a-2b+3c),\\
B^{-1}(a,b,c)&=(a+2b-2c,\ 2a+b-2c,\ -2a-2b+3c),\\
C^{-1}(a,b,c)&=(-a-2b+2c,\ 2a+b-2c,\ -2a-2b+3c).
\end{aligned}
\]
These preserve the cone (a linear-combination identity on $Q$) and preserve primitivity:
the gcd $g$ of the legs satisfies $g^2\mid c^2$, hence $g\mid c$, so a common factor of a
parent's legs would divide the child's. One shows that for any primitive triple with odd
first leg other than $\bfr$, at least one inverse produces an admissible primitive triple
of \emph{strictly smaller} hypotenuse. Fermat descent on the hypotenuse terminates only at
$\bfr$, and reading the descent backwards produces $W$. Formally one proves by strong
induction on $N$ the statement ``every admissible primitive triple with odd first leg and
hypotenuse at most $N$ lies in the tree''.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Star location]\label{thm:location}
Every primitive Pythagorean triple $(a,b,c)$ with positive entries and odd $a$ is a star
centre: there is a word $W$ with $W\bfr=(a,b,c)$ and
$\dirp(W\!A\,C^j\bfr)\to(a/c,\,b/c)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Spoke charge]
For admissible $p$ and $d>0$, say $d$ is a \emph{spoke charge at $p$} if there is a family
$(w_j)$ of admissible triples with $\ip{w_j}{p}=-d$ for all $j$ and $c_{w_j}\to\infty$.
By Theorem~\ref{thm:star} every spoke charge is drawn as a genuine curve into $\dirp p$;
by Theorem~\ref{thm:ratio} distinct charges give visibly distinct curves.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:treespoke}
Put $T_{n,j}:=C^jA^n\bfr$. Then $T_{n,j}=\eu\bigl(n+2+2j(n+1),\ n+1\bigr)$; it is
admissible, has charge $2(n+1)^2$ at $e_1$ independently of $j$, and $c_{T_{n,j}}\ge j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:abranch} gives $A^n\bfr=\eu(n+2,n+1)$, Remark~\ref{rem:cfrozen} gives the
$C$-iterate, and Theorem~\ref{thm:euch} the charge.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Transport of spokes]\label{thm:transport}
If $d$ is a spoke charge at $p$ and $W$ is a word in the generators, then $d$ is a spoke
charge at $Wp$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply $W$ to the witnessing family: charge is preserved by isometry, admissibility by
Proposition~\ref{prop:adm}, and the hypotenuse does not decrease.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Infinite multiplicity]\label{thm:mult}
The set of spoke charges at $e_1$ is infinite, containing $2(n+1)^2$ for every $n\ge0$.
Consequently, for every node $W\bfr$ of the tree --- and hence, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:complete}, for every primitive Pythagorean triple with positive entries
and odd first leg --- the set of spoke charges is infinite. Every star has infinitely many
distinct spokes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first claim is Lemma~\ref{lem:treespoke}. For the second, take $W'=W\!A$, so that
$W'e_1=W\bfr$, and transport by Theorem~\ref{thm:transport}; injectivity of
$n\mapsto2(n+1)^2$ keeps the charges distinct.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Tree spoke spectrum]\label{thm:treespec}
A positive integer $d$ arises as the charge at $(1,0)$ of an unbounded family of
\emph{tree nodes} if and only if $d=2n^2$ for some $n\ge1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
($\Rightarrow$) Every tree node is $\eu(m,n)$ with $0<n<m$, starting from $\eu(2,1)$ and
using Theorem~\ref{thm:eu}; its charge is $2n^2$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:euch}.
($\Leftarrow$) Given $n\ge1$, write $n=k+1$ and use $\bigl(C^jA^{k}\bfr\bigr)_{j\ge0}$
from Lemma~\ref{lem:treespoke}.
\end{proof}

Together with Corollary~\ref{cor:spectrum} this pins the star at $(1,0)$ down completely:
the drawn spokes are labelled $2,8,18,32,50,\dots$

\section{Escape rate for mixed addresses}

\begin{definition}
Let $g=g_1\cdots g_\ell$ be a word in $\{A,B,C\}$; write $|g|=\ell$ and $\#_B(g)$ for the
number of occurrences of $B$, and let $g\cdot\bfr$ be the resulting node.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Per-letter bounds]\label{lem:letter}
For admissible $v$ and any letter $X$: $c_v\le c_{Xv}\le7c_v$; and $c_{Bv}\ge3c_v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Since $a,b\le c$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:adm}), each generator's third coordinate --- of
the shape $\pm2a\pm2b+3c$ --- lies between $c$ and $7c$; and $2a+2b+3c\ge3c$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Two-sided Lyapunov bound]\label{thm:lyap}
For every address $g$,
\[
5\cdot3^{\#_B(g)}\ \le\ c(g\cdot\bfr)\ \le\ 5\cdot7^{|g|} .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Induct on the word using Lemma~\ref{lem:letter}, with $c(\bfr)=5$.
\end{proof}

Exponential escape to the boundary is therefore forced by a positive density of $B$'s in
the address: a $B$-free branch is trapped in the parabolic, polynomial regime. The same
alphabet records the effect of each letter on the spoke index: reading a word from the
root, the spoke index is frozen by $C$ (Remark~\ref{rem:cfrozen}) and refreshed to the
larger parameter by $A$ and $B$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:eu}).

\section{Algorithms}

\begin{algorithmbox}[Tree generation to a hypotenuse bound]\label{alg:gen}
Breadth-first expansion of the root by the three generators, pruning nodes with hypotenuse
exceeding $N$. Since each generator strictly increases the hypotenuse on admissible nodes
with positive legs, the search terminates, and by Theorem~\ref{thm:complete} it enumerates
exactly the primitive triples with odd first leg and hypotenuse at most $N$, each once.
Cost $O(|\mathcal T_N|)$, with $|\mathcal T_N|\sim N/(2\pi)$.
\end{algorithmbox}

\begin{algorithmbox}[Descent / address recovery]
Given a primitive triple with odd first leg, apply the inverse generator yielding an
admissible primitive triple of smaller hypotenuse; repeat until the root, then reverse the
letters. Correctness and termination are Theorem~\ref{thm:complete}; by
Theorem~\ref{thm:lyap} the number of steps is at most
$\log_3(c/5)+\#\{\text{non-}B\text{ letters}\}$, and $O(\log c)$ for balanced addresses.
\end{algorithmbox}

\begin{algorithmbox}[Spoke extraction and tangency check]
Given a target primitive triple $p$ and a bound $D$, bucket the nodes of Algorithm~\ref{alg:gen} by
charge $d=-\ip{v}{p}$. Buckets with $d\le D$ and many members are the visible spokes at
$p$. For each, the quantity $c_v\|\dirp v-\dirp p\|^2$ must equal $2d/c_p$ \emph{exactly}
(Theorem~\ref{thm:tangency}), a strong numerical check on the whole theory.
\end{algorithmbox}

\section{Applications and context}

\textbf{Thin groups and local--global phenomena.} The Berggren monoid sits inside
$O(2,1;\Z)$ and its orbit is a Zariski-dense but arithmetically thin subset of the light
cone. Structurally the picture is the analogue of an Apollonian circle packing, where an
infinite-index subgroup of $O(3,1;\Z)$ produces a fractal boundary set whose integer
curvature data satisfy delicate local-to-global rules. Corollary~\ref{cor:spectrum} is the
Pythagorean version of an Apollonian local--global statement --- and, unlike the
Apollonian case, it is complete and elementary.

\smallskip
\noindent\textbf{Visualisation as an oracle.} Each visible feature corresponds to a
theorem: bundles $\leftrightarrow$ horocycles (Theorem~\ref{thm:star}); bending into the
rim $\leftrightarrow$ contact order two (Corollary~\ref{cor:contact}); discreteness of
spokes $\leftrightarrow$ charge quantization (Theorem~\ref{thm:quant}); streaks
$\leftrightarrow$ hyperbolic geodesics with exponential escape (Theorem~\ref{thm:exp});
absence of a star at $\pi/4$ $\leftrightarrow$ irrationality (Theorem~\ref{thm:irr});
ubiquity of stars $\leftrightarrow$ transport, completeness and density
(Theorems~\ref{thm:location}, \ref{thm:dense}).

\smallskip
\noindent\textbf{Structured integer sequence generation.} Theorem~\ref{thm:lyap} allows
generating triples of prescribed hypotenuse magnitude by choosing an address with the
right number of $B$'s, and of prescribed proximity to a target boundary direction by
choosing a trailing block of $C$'s: a controllable generator of structured integer data
whose difficulty parameter and geometric parameter are independently tunable.

\section{Discussion and future directions}

\subsection{What is settled}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.4em]
  \item \emph{Uniform tangency law.} Resolved in exact form: the product
        $c_v\|\dirp v-\dirp p\|^2$ is literally constant
        (Theorem~\ref{thm:tangency}), and the contact order is exactly two
        (Corollary~\ref{cor:contact}).
  \item \emph{Escape-rate dichotomy for mixed addresses.} Partially resolved:
        Theorem~\ref{thm:lyap} gives $5\cdot3^{\#_B}\le c\le5\cdot7^{|g|}$. The
        rationality/irrationality classification of the limit of a general infinite
        address is open.
  \item \emph{Star centres with multiplicity.} The multiplicity half is resolved
        (Theorem~\ref{thm:mult}), and at $(1,0)$ the spectrum is exactly
        $\{2n^2:n\ge1\}$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:treespec}). What remains open is the
        complementary ``at most one curve at a generic irrational point''.
  \item \emph{Charge--depth law.} Resolved in corrected form: the universal
        $\Theta(\log n)$ claim is false (Theorem~\ref{thm:abranch}); the correct
        statement is Theorem~\ref{thm:depth} with the attaining Pell family
        (Theorem~\ref{thm:pell}).
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Open problems}

\begin{conjecture}[Spectral rigidity]
Let $M$ be a submonoid of $\langle A,B,C\rangle$ and $S(M)\subseteq\Z_{>0}$ the set of
charges realised at $(1,0)$ by the orbit $M\cdot\bfr$. Then $S(M)=\{2n^2:n\ge1\}$ if and
only if $M$ has finite index in the full monoid; and every thin submonoid satisfies
$\#\{d\in S(M):d\le X\}=o(\sqrt X)$.
\end{conjecture}

The reason to expect this is Theorem~\ref{thm:euch} together with Theorem~\ref{thm:eu}:
the charge of a node is $2n^2$ where $n$ is its smaller Euclid parameter, and the
parameter pair evolves by the ternary tree on coprime pairs; so $S(M)$ is the image of the
parameter tree under a submonoid, and counting it is an Apollonian-style local--global
statistic transplanted to the Pythagorean setting.

\begin{conjecture}[Limit classification for infinite addresses]
For an infinite address $g_1g_2g_3\cdots$ the plotted points converge to an ideal point
$\xi$; then $\xi$ is rational if and only if the address is eventually a word in
$\{A,C\}$, and otherwise $\xi$ is irrational with a continued-fraction-type expansion read
off the address.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{conjecture}[Generic simplicity]
At an ideal point that is not a primitive rational direction, the plot carries at most one
accumulating curve; equivalently, a Lebesgue-generic boundary point receives no star.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{conjecture}[Counting spokes by depth]
Let $N(k)$ be the number of distinct spoke charges at $(1,0)$ realised by nodes of depth
at most $k$. Theorems~\ref{thm:depth}--\ref{thm:abranch} give
$\Omega(k)\le N(k)\le O(3^k)$; determine the true order of growth.
\end{conjecture}

\subsection{A wider programme}
The Euclid-parameter picture recasts the story as a dynamical system on coprime pairs with
the charge a quadratic form on that system. Analogous statements should hold for other
Lorentzian lattices: replacing $a^2+b^2-c^2$ by an indefinite ternary quadratic form of
class number one, one expects an analogous tree, an analogous star picture at rational
ideal points, and a quantization theorem whose spectrum is dictated by the genus theory of
the form.

\section{Summary of main results}

\begin{longtable}{@{}p{0.30\textwidth}p{0.62\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule

\midrule
\endhead

  "demo": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Stars on the Rim: numerical demonstrations of the boundary geometry of the
Berggren (Barning-Hall) tree of primitive Pythagorean triples.

This script is fully self-contained (standard library only) and verifies, by
exact integer / high-precision arithmetic, every quantitative claim of the
accompanying article and paper:

  1. The three Berggren generators are integral Lorentz isometries of
     Q(a,b,c) = a^2 + b^2 - c^2, and the tree they generate consists of
     primitive Pythagorean triples with odd first leg.

  2. The chord-charge identity
         ||dir v - dir p||^2 = -2 <v,p> / (c_v c_p).

  3. The exact tangency law: c_v * ||dir v - dir p||^2 = 2d/c_p is CONSTANT
     along a horocycle of charge d, so the contact order with the boundary
     circle is exactly two.

  4. Charge quantization: the charge c-a of a primitive triple is twice a
     square (odd first leg) or an odd square (even first leg); inside the tree
     the spectrum is exactly {2n^2 : n >= 1}.

  5. The Euclid dictionary A:(m,n)->(2m-n,m), B:(m,n)->(2m+n,m),
     C:(m,n)->(m+2n,n), and the identification "spoke index = smaller Euclid
     parameter".

  6. The escape-rate dichotomy: the parabolic branch approaches its boundary
     point at rate Theta(k^-2), the hyperbolic one at rate O(3^-k), with the
     explicit constants 2/(17 k^2) and 1/(5 * 3^k) at the root.

  7. Star location and multiplicity: every node is a star centre, and each
     star carries infinitely many distinct spokes.

  8. The two-sided Lyapunov bound 5 * 3^{#B} <= c <= 5 * 7^{len}.

Run:  python3 demo.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from decimal import Decimal, getcontext
from fractions import Fraction
from math import gcd, isqrt
from typing import Dict, Iterable, Iterator, List, Sequence, Tuple

getcontext().prec = 60

Triple = Tuple[int, int, int]

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. The Lorentzian setup
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT: Triple = (3, 4, 5)
E1: Triple = (1, 0, 1)  # ideal point (1, 0)
E2: Triple = (0, 1, 1)  # ideal point (0, 1)


def bil(v: Triple, w: Triple) -> int:
    """Minkowski product <v,w> = v1 w1 + v2 w2 - v3 w3 of signature (2,1)."""
    return v[0] * w[0] + v[1] * w[1] - v[2] * w[2]


def qform(v: Triple) -> int:
    """The quadratic form Q(a,b,c) = a^2 + b^2 - c^2."""
    return bil(v, v)


def gen_A(v: Triple) -> Triple:
    a, b, c = v
    return (a - 2 * b + 2 * c, 2 * a - b + 2 * c, 2 * a - 2 * b + 3 * c)


def gen_B(v: Triple) -> Triple:
    a, b, c = v
    return (a + 2 * b + 2 * c, 2 * a + b + 2 * c, 2 * a + 2 * b + 3 * c)


def gen_C(v: Triple) -> Triple:
    a, b, c = v
    return (-a + 2 * b + 2 * c, -2 * a + b + 2 * c, -2 * a + 2 * b + 3 * c)


GENERATORS = {"A": gen_A, "B": gen_B, "C": gen_C}


def inv_A(v: Triple) -> Triple:
    a, b, c = v
    return (a + 2 * b - 2 * c, -2 * a - b + 2 * c, -2 * a - 2 * b + 3 * c)


def inv_B(v: Triple) -> Triple:
    a, b, c = v
    return (a + 2 * b - 2 * c, 2 * a + b - 2 * c, -2 * a - 2 * b + 3 * c)


def inv_C(v: Triple) -> Triple:
    a, b, c = v
    return (-a - 2 * b + 2 * c, 2 * a + b - 2 * c, -2 * a - 2 * b + 3 * c)


INVERSES = {"A": inv_A, "B": inv_B, "C": inv_C}


def apply_word(word: str, v: Triple = ROOT) -> Triple:
    """Apply the letters of `word` left-to-right, starting at `v`."""
    for letter in word:
        v = GENERATORS[letter](v)
    return v


def dir_point(v: Triple) -> Tuple[Fraction, Fraction]:
    """The ideal point (a/c, b/c) on the unit circle."""
    a, b, c = v
    return (Fraction(a, c), Fraction(b, c))


def chord_sq(v: Triple, p: Triple) -> Fraction:
    """Exact squared chordal distance between the two plotted ideal points."""
    xv, yv = dir_point(v)
    xp, yp = dir_point(p)
    return (xv - xp) ** 2 + (yv - yp) ** 2


def charge(v: Triple, p: Triple) -> int:
    """The Lorentz charge d = -<v,p> of v at the null vector p."""
    return -bil(v, p)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Euclid coordinates
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def eu(m: int, n: int) -> Triple:
    """Euclid parametrisation (m^2-n^2, 2mn, m^2+n^2)."""
    return (m * m - n * n, 2 * m * n, m * m + n * n)


def euclid_params(v: Triple) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """Recover (m,n) with 0 < n < m from a primitive triple with odd first leg."""
    a, _, c = v
    m_sq = (c + a) // 2
    n_sq = (c - a) // 2
    m, n = isqrt(m_sq), isqrt(n_sq)
    assert m * m == m_sq and n * n == n_sq, "not a primitive odd-leg triple"
    return m, n


def spoke_index(v: Triple) -> int:
    """The spoke index of a node = its smaller Euclid parameter."""
    return euclid_params(v)[1]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Tree enumeration
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def tree_nodes(max_hyp: int) -> List[Tuple[str, Triple]]:
    """All (address, triple) with hypotenuse <= max_hyp, breadth-first."""
    out: List[Tuple[str, Triple]] = []
    frontier: List[Tuple[str, Triple]] = [("", ROOT)]
    while frontier:
        nxt: List[Tuple[str, Triple]] = []
        for word, v in frontier:
            if v[2] > max_hyp:
                continue
            out.append((word, v))
            for letter, g in GENERATORS.items():
                child = g(v)
                if child[2] <= max_hyp:
                    nxt.append((word + letter, child))
        frontier = nxt
    return out


def all_primitive_odd_leg(max_hyp: int) -> List[Triple]:
    """Brute-force list of primitive triples with odd first leg, c <= max_hyp."""
    found: List[Triple] = []
    for a in range(1, max_hyp + 1, 2):
        for b in range(1, max_hyp + 1):
            s = a * a + b * b
            c = isqrt(s)
            if c * c == s and c <= max_hyp and gcd(a, b) == 1:
                found.append((a, b, c))
    return sorted(found)


def descend(v: Triple) -> str:
    """Recover the address of a primitive odd-leg triple by Fermat descent."""
    letters: List[str] = []
    while v != ROOT:
        for name, inv in INVERSES.items():
            w = inv(v)
            if w[0] > 0 and w[1] > 0 and 0 < w[2] < v[2] and qform(w) == 0:
                letters.append(name)
                v = w
                break
        else:  # pragma: no cover - unreachable by completeness
            raise RuntimeError(f"descent stuck at {v}")
    return "".join(reversed(letters))

def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)


def check(label: str, condition: bool) -> None:
    status = "OK " if condition else "FAIL"
    print(f"  [{status}] {label}")
    assert condition, label

def demo_lorentz() -> None:
    banner("1.  The Berggren generators lie in O(2,1;Z)")
    probes: List[Triple] = [(3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (1, 0, 1), (2, -7, 11), (0, 1, 1)]
    for name, g in GENERATORS.items():
        ok = all(bil(g(v), g(w)) == bil(v, w) for v in probes for w in probes)
        check(f"generator {name} preserves the Minkowski product", ok)
    print()
    print("  Root and its three children (all on the light cone):")
    for name, g in GENERATORS.items():
        child = g(ROOT)
        print(f"    {name}(3,4,5) = {child}   Q = {qform(child)}")
    print()
    print("  Conserved charges of each generator:")
    v = (20, 21, 29)
    print(f"    v            = {v}")
    print(f"    C conserves c-a : {v[2]-v[0]} -> {gen_C(v)[2]-gen_C(v)[0]}")
    print(f"    A conserves c-b : {v[2]-v[1]} -> {gen_A(v)[2]-gen_A(v)[1]}")
    print(f"    B negates  a-b  : {v[0]-v[1]} -> {gen_B(v)[0]-gen_B(v)[1]}")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demo 2 : the chord-charge identity
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_chord_charge() -> None:
    banner("2.  Chord = charge:  ||dir v - dir p||^2 = -2<v,p>/(c_v c_p)")
    nodes = [v for _, v in tree_nodes(400)]
    centres: List[Triple] = [E1, E2, ROOT, (5, 12, 13), (15, 8, 17)]
    ok = True
    for p in centres:
        for v in nodes:
            lhs = chord_sq(v, p)
            rhs = Fraction(-2 * bil(v, p), v[2] * p[2])
            ok = ok and lhs == rhs
    check(f"identity holds exactly for {len(nodes)} nodes x {len(centres)} centres", ok)
    print()
    print("  Sample (star centre p = (1,0,1), i.e. the boundary point (1,0)):")
    print(f"    {'node':>18} {'d = c-a':>8}  {'||dir v - (1,0)||^2':>22}")
    for v in nodes[:8]:
        print(f"    {str(v):>18} {charge(v, E1):>8}  {str(chord_sq(v, E1)):>22}")

# Demo 3 : exact tangency, contact order two

def demo_tangency() -> None:
    banner("3.  Exact tangency law:  c_v * ||dir v - dir p||^2 = 2d/c_p  (CONSTANT)")
    p = E1
    print("  Spoke of charge d = 2n^2 at (1,0) is the family eu(m,n), m = n+1, n+2, ...")
    print()
    for n in (1, 2, 3, 5):
        d = 2 * n * n
        print(f"  spoke index n = {n},  charge d = {d},  predicted 2d/c_p = {2*d}")
        row = []
        for m in range(n + 1, n + 7):
            v = eu(m, n)
            row.append(v[2] * chord_sq(v, p))
        check(f"    product constant along the spoke  ({row[0]})",
              all(x == Fraction(2 * d) for x in row))
    print()
    print("  Contact order is exactly two:  c^2 * chord^2 -> infinity,  sqrt(c) * chord^2 -> 0")
    n = 2
    print(f"    {'m':>6} {'c':>10} {'c^2*chord^2':>16} {'sqrt(c)*chord^2':>18}")
    for m in (3, 10, 100, 1000, 10000):
        v = eu(m, n)
        ch = chord_sq(v, p)
        big = Decimal(v[2]) ** 2 * Decimal(ch.numerator) / Decimal(ch.denominator)
        small = Decimal(v[2]).sqrt() * Decimal(ch.numerator) / Decimal(ch.denominator)
        print(f"    {m:>6} {v[2]:>10} {big:>16.4f} {small:>18.8f}")

# Demo 4 : charge quantization
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def is_twice_square(d: int) -> bool:
    return d % 2 == 0 and isqrt(d // 2) ** 2 == d // 2


def is_odd_square(d: int) -> bool:
    r = isqrt(d)
    return r * r == d and r % 2 == 1


def demo_quantization() -> None:
    banner("4.  Charge quantization:  c - a is twice a square, or an odd square")
    N = 400
    triples = [t for t in all_primitive_odd_leg(N)]
    odd_first = [t for t in triples if t[0] % 2 == 1]
    even_first = [(b, a, c) for (a, b, c) in triples if b % 2 == 0]  # swap legs
    check("odd first leg  =>  c-a = 2n^2",
          all(is_twice_square(c - a) for a, _, c in odd_first))
    check("even first leg =>  c-a = odd square",
          all(is_odd_square(c - a) for a, _, c in even_first))

    seen_odd = sorted({c - a for a, _, c in odd_first})
    seen_even = sorted({c - a for a, _, c in even_first})
    print()
    print(f"  charges realised with ODD  first leg (c <= {N}):  {seen_odd[:12]} ...")
    print(f"  charges realised with EVEN first leg (c <= {N}):  {seen_even[:12]} ...")
    print(f"  first twelve values of 2n^2                    :  "
          f"{[2*n*n for n in range(1, 13)]}")
    print(f"  first twelve odd squares                       :  "
          f"{[(2*m-1)**2 for m in range(1, 13)]}")
    print()
    print("  Realisability (every admissible charge occurs):")
    for n in range(1, 5):
        t = (2 * n + 1, 2 * n * n + 2 * n, 2 * n * n + 2 * n + 1)
        check(f"    (2n+1, 2n^2+2n, 2n^2+2n+1) with n={n} -> {t}, charge {t[2]-t[0]} = 2*{n}^2",
              qform(t) == 0 and gcd(t[0], t[1]) == 1 and t[2] - t[0] == 2 * n * n)
    for m in range(1, 5):
        t = (4 * m, 4 * m * m - 1, 4 * m * m + 1)
        check(f"    (4m, 4m^2-1, 4m^2+1) with m={m} -> {t}, charge {t[2]-t[0]} = ({2*m-1})^2",
              qform(t) == 0 and gcd(t[0], t[1]) == 1 and t[2] - t[0] == (2 * m - 1) ** 2)
    print()
    print("  Density-zero check: #{admissible charges <= X} grows like ~1.2 sqrt(X)")
    for X in (100, 1000, 10000, 100000):
        cnt = sum(1 for d in range(1, X + 1) if is_twice_square(d) or is_odd_square(d))
        print(f"    X = {X:>7}:  count = {cnt:>5}   count/sqrt(X) = {cnt / X**0.5:.4f}")

def demo_euclid() -> None:
    banner("5.  Euclid coordinates:  A:(m,n)->(2m-n,m)  B:(m,n)->(2m+n,m)  C:(m,n)->(m+2n,n)")
    pairs = [(2, 1), (5, 2), (7, 4), (11, 3)]
    for (m, n) in pairs:
        v = eu(m, n)
        check(f"  A on eu({m},{n})", gen_A(v) == eu(2 * m - n, m))
        check(f"  B on eu({m},{n})", gen_B(v) == eu(2 * m + n, m))
        check(f"  C on eu({m},{n})", gen_C(v) == eu(m + 2 * n, n))
        check(f"  charge at (1,0) is 2*{n}^2 = {2*n*n}", charge(v, E1) == 2 * n * n)
        check(f"  charge at (0,1) is ({m}-{n})^2 = {(m-n)**2}", charge(v, E2) == (m - n) ** 2)
    print()
    print("  The three pure branches from the root, with their spoke indices:")
    print(f"    {'k':>3} | {'A^k root':>22} idx | {'B^k root':>26} idx | {'C^k root':>22} idx")
    va = vb = vc = ROOT
    for k in range(6):
        print(f"    {k:>3} | {str(va):>22} {spoke_index(va):>3} | "
              f"{str(vb):>26} {spoke_index(vb):>3} | {str(vc):>22} {spoke_index(vc):>3}")
        va, vb, vc = gen_A(va), gen_B(vb), gen_C(vc)
    print()
    print("  A-branch index = k+1 (slowest);  C-branch index frozen at 1 (one spoke);")
    print("  B-branch index = Pell number 1,2,5,12,29,70 (fastest), with 2^k <= n < 2*3^k:")
    pell = [1, 2]
    while len(pell) < 8:
        pell.append(2 * pell[-1] + pell[-2])
    print(f"    {'k':>3} {'2^k':>8} {'Pell_k':>8} {'2*3^k':>8}")
    for k in range(8):
        print(f"    {k:>3} {2**k:>8} {pell[k]:>8} {2*3**k:>8}")
        check(f"    sandwich at k={k}", (k == 0) or (2**k <= pell[k] < 2 * 3**k))

def demo_dichotomy() -> None:
    banner("6.  Escape-rate dichotomy:  parabolic Theta(k^-2)  vs  hyperbolic O(3^-k)")
    sqrt2_over_2 = Decimal(2).sqrt() / 2
    print(f"    {'k':>3} | {'1 - x(C^k r)':>16} {'2/(17k^2)':>14} | "
          f"{'|x(B^k r)-r2/2|':>18} {'1/(5*3^k)':>14}")
    vc = vb = ROOT
    for k in range(1, 10):
        vc, vb = gen_C(vc), gen_B(vb)
        xc = Decimal(vc[0]) / Decimal(vc[2])
        xb = Decimal(vb[0]) / Decimal(vb[2])
        lhs_c = 1 - xc
        bound_c = Decimal(2) / Decimal(17 * k * k)
        lhs_b = abs(xb - sqrt2_over_2)
        bound_b = Decimal(1) / Decimal(5 * 3 ** k)
        print(f"    {k:>3} | {lhs_c:>16.10f} {bound_c:>14.10f} | "
              f"{lhs_b:>18.14f} {bound_b:>14.10f}")
        check(f"    parabolic lower bound at k={k}", lhs_c >= bound_c)
        check(f"    hyperbolic upper bound at k={k}", lhs_b <= bound_b)
    print()
    print("  Irrationality obstruction: x(v) = a/c is always rational, but the")
    print("  hyperbolic limit is sqrt(2)/2, irrational.  Hence NO triple is ever")
    print("  plotted at angle pi/4: there is no star there, only one geodesic.")
    print(f"    sqrt(2)/2 = {sqrt2_over_2}")
    print(f"    closest tree node within c <= 5000 : ", end="")
    best = min((v for _, v in tree_nodes(5000)),
               key=lambda v: abs(Decimal(v[0]) / Decimal(v[2]) - sqrt2_over_2))
    print(f"{best},  x = {Decimal(best[0])/Decimal(best[2]):.14f}")

def demo_stars() -> None:
    banner("7.  A star at every node, each with infinitely many spokes")
    print("  Transport identities that move the star around the tree:")
    check(f"    A(1,0,1) = (3,4,5)", gen_A(E1) == ROOT)
    check(f"    B(1,0,1) = (3,4,5)", gen_B(E1) == ROOT)
    check(f"    C(1,0,1) = (1,0,1)", gen_C(E1) == E1)
    print()
    print("  The tree spokes T(n,j) = C^j A^n root at the ideal point (1,0):")
    print("  (row n is one spoke; the charge is constant along a row and equals 2(n+1)^2)")
    for n in range(4):
        v = ROOT
        for _ in range(n):
            v = gen_A(v)
        row: List[Triple] = []
        w = v
        for _ in range(4):
            row.append(w)
            w = gen_C(w)
        charges = {charge(t, E1) for t in row}
        print(f"    n={n}: charge {charges.pop():>3}   " +
              "  ".join(str(t) for t in row))
    print()
    print("  Star at the ROOT (3,4,5): the family A C^j (3,4,5) converges to (3/5,4/5)")
    print(f"    {'j':>3} {'node':>28} {'dir x':>14} {'dir y':>14}")
    w = ROOT
    for j in range(7):
        node = gen_A(w)
        x, y = dir_point(node)
        print(f"    {j:>3} {str(node):>28} {float(x):>14.9f} {float(y):>14.9f}")
        check(f"      charge 2 at the root", charge(node, ROOT) == 2)
        w = gen_C(w)
    print(f"    limit                                {3/5:>14.9f} {4/5:>14.9f}")
    print()
    print("  Quantitative separation of spokes:")
    print("    at EQUAL hypotenuse the squared chordal distances are in the ratio d/d'.")
    # eu(8,1) = (63,16,65) and eu(7,4) = (33,56,65): same hypotenuse, different charge.
    v1, v2 = eu(8, 1), eu(7, 4)
    d1, d2 = charge(v1, E1), charge(v2, E1)
    print(f"      eu(8,1) = {v1}, c = {v1[2]}, charge d  = {d1}")
    print(f"      eu(7,4) = {v2}, c = {v2[2]}, charge d' = {d2}")
    check(f"      equal hypotenuse", v1[2] == v2[2])
    r_chord = chord_sq(v1, E1) / chord_sq(v2, E1)
    check(f"      chord^2 ratio {r_chord} equals d/d' = {Fraction(d1, d2)}",
          r_chord == Fraction(d1, d2))

def demo_completeness_and_growth() -> None:
    banner("8.  Completeness of the tree, and the two-sided Lyapunov bound")
    N = 300
    from_tree = sorted(v for _, v in tree_nodes(N))
    brute = sorted(t for t in all_primitive_odd_leg(N) if t[0] % 2 == 1)
    check(f"tree with c <= {N} equals the brute-force list "
          f"({len(from_tree)} vs {len(brute)} triples)", from_tree == brute)
    print()
    print("  Address recovery by Fermat descent:")
    for t in [(3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (21, 20, 29), (119, 120, 169), (33, 56, 65)]:
        w = descend(t)
        check(f"    {str(t):>16} -> address {w!r:>10}  (round-trip)",
              apply_word(w) == t)
    print()
    print("  Lyapunov sandwich  5*3^{#B} <= c <= 5*7^{len}:")
    print(f"    {'address':>10} {'5*3^#B':>10} {'c':>12} {'5*7^len':>12}")
    for w in ["", "A", "B", "C", "ABC", "BBC", "CCC", "BABC", "BBBB", "CCCCC"]:
        v = apply_word(w)
        lo = 5 * 3 ** w.count("B")
        hi = 5 * 7 ** len(w)
        print(f"    {w!r:>10} {lo:>10} {v[2]:>12} {hi:>12}")
        check(f"      sandwich for {w!r}", lo <= v[2] <= hi)
    print()
    print("  Spoke index vs depth:  n < 2*3^depth, universally.")
    print(f"    {'depth':>6} {'max index seen':>16} {'2*3^depth':>12}")
    by_depth: Dict[int, int] = {}
    for word, v in tree_nodes(2 * 10 ** 6):
        d = len(word)
        by_depth[d] = max(by_depth.get(d, 0), spoke_index(v))
    for d in sorted(by_depth)[:9]:
        print(f"    {d:>6} {by_depth[d]:>16} {2*3**d:>12}")
        check(f"      bound at depth {d}", by_depth[d] < 2 * 3 ** d)

from __future__ import annotations

from decimal import Decimal, getcontext
from fractions import Fraction
from math import gcd, isqrt
from typing import Dict, Iterable, Iterator, List, Sequence, Tuple

getcontext().prec = 60

Triple = Tuple[int, int, int]

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. The Lorentzian setup
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT: Triple = (3, 4, 5)
E1: Triple = (1, 0, 1)  # ideal point (1, 0)
E2: Triple = (0, 1, 1)  # ideal point (0, 1)


def bil(v: Triple, w: Triple) -> int:
    """Minkowski product <v,w> = v1 w1 + v2 w2 - v3 w3 of signature (2,1)."""
    return v[0] * w[0] + v[1] * w[1] - v[2] * w[2]


def qform(v: Triple) -> int:
    """The quadratic form Q(a,b,c) = a^2 + b^2 - c^2."""
    return bil(v, v)


def gen_A(v: Triple) -> Triple:
    a, b, c = v
    return (a - 2 * b + 2 * c, 2 * a - b + 2 * c, 2 * a - 2 * b + 3 * c)


def gen_B(v: Triple) -> Triple:
    a, b, c = v
    return (a + 2 * b + 2 * c, 2 * a + b + 2 * c, 2 * a + 2 * b + 3 * c)


def gen_C(v: Triple) -> Triple:
    a, b, c = v
    return (-a + 2 * b + 2 * c, -2 * a + b + 2 * c, -2 * a + 2 * b + 3 * c)


GENERATORS = {"A": gen_A, "B": gen_B, "C": gen_C}


def inv_A(v: Triple) -> Triple:
    a, b, c = v
    return (a + 2 * b - 2 * c, -2 * a - b + 2 * c, -2 * a - 2 * b + 3 * c)


def inv_B(v: Triple) -> Triple:
    a, b, c = v
    return (a + 2 * b - 2 * c, 2 * a + b - 2 * c, -2 * a - 2 * b + 3 * c)


def inv_C(v: Triple) -> Triple:
    a, b, c = v
    return (-a - 2 * b + 2 * c, 2 * a + b - 2 * c, -2 * a - 2 * b + 3 * c)


INVERSES = {"A": inv_A, "B": inv_B, "C": inv_C}


def apply_word(word: str, v: Triple = ROOT) -> Triple:
    """Apply the letters of `word` left-to-right, starting at `v`."""
    for letter in word:
        v = GENERATORS[letter](v)
    return v


def dir_point(v: Triple) -> Tuple[Fraction, Fraction]:
    """The ideal point (a/c, b/c) on the unit circle."""
    a, b, c = v
    return (Fraction(a, c), Fraction(b, c))


def chord_sq(v: Triple, p: Triple) -> Fraction:
    """Exact squared chordal distance between the two plotted ideal points."""
    xv, yv = dir_point(v)
    xp, yp = dir_point(p)
    return (xv - xp) ** 2 + (yv - yp) ** 2


def charge(v: Triple, p: Triple) -> int:
    """The Lorentz charge d = -<v,p> of v at the null vector p."""
    return -bil(v, p)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Euclid coordinates
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def eu(m: int, n: int) -> Triple:
    """Euclid parametrisation (m^2-n^2, 2mn, m^2+n^2)."""
    return (m * m - n * n, 2 * m * n, m * m + n * n)


def euclid_params(v: Triple) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """Recover (m,n) with 0 < n < m from a primitive triple with odd first leg."""
    a, _, c = v
    m_sq = (c + a) // 2
    n_sq = (c - a) // 2
    m, n = isqrt(m_sq), isqrt(n_sq)
    assert m * m == m_sq and n * n == n_sq, "not a primitive odd-leg triple"
    return m, n


def spoke_index(v: Triple) -> int:
    """The spoke index of a node = its smaller Euclid parameter."""
    return euclid_params(v)[1]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Tree enumeration
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def tree_nodes(max_hyp: int) -> List[Tuple[str, Triple]]:
    """All (address, triple) with hypotenuse <= max_hyp, breadth-first."""
    out: List[Tuple[str, Triple]] = []
    frontier: List[Tuple[str, Triple]] = [("", ROOT)]
    while frontier:
        nxt: List[Tuple[str, Triple]] = []
        for word, v in frontier:
            if v[2] > max_hyp:
                continue
            out.append((word, v))
            for letter, g in GENERATORS.items():
                child = g(v)
                if child[2] <= max_hyp:
                    nxt.append((word + letter, child))
        frontier = nxt
    return out


def all_primitive_odd_leg(max_hyp: int) -> List[Triple]:
    """Brute-force list of primitive triples with odd first leg, c <= max_hyp."""
    found: List[Triple] = []
    for a in range(1, max_hyp + 1, 2):
        for b in range(1, max_hyp + 1):
            s = a * a + b * b
            c = isqrt(s)
            if c * c == s and c <= max_hyp and gcd(a, b) == 1:
                found.append((a, b, c))
    return sorted(found)


def descend(v: Triple) -> str:
    """Recover the address of a primitive odd-leg triple by Fermat descent."""
    letters: List[str] = []
    while v != ROOT:
        for name, inv in INVERSES.items():
            w = inv(v)
            if w[0] > 0 and w[1] > 0 and 0 < w[2] < v[2] and qform(w) == 0:
                letters.append(name)
                v = w
                break
        else:  # pragma: no cover - unreachable by completeness
            raise RuntimeError(f"descent stuck at {v}")
    return "".join(reversed(letters))

def is_twice_square(d: int) -> bool:
    return d % 2 == 0 and isqrt(d // 2) ** 2 == d // 2


def is_odd_square(d: int) -> bool:
    r = isqrt(d)
    return r * r == d and r % 2 == 1


def demo_quantization() -> None:
    banner("4.  Charge quantization:  c - a is twice a square, or an odd square")
    N = 400
    triples = [t for t in all_primitive_odd_leg(N)]
    odd_first = [t for t in triples if t[0] % 2 == 1]
    even_first = [(b, a, c) for (a, b, c) in triples if b % 2 == 0]  # swap legs
    check("odd first leg  =>  c-a = 2n^2",
          all(is_twice_square(c - a) for a, _, c in odd_first))
    check("even first leg =>  c-a = odd square",
          all(is_odd_square(c - a) for a, _, c in even_first))

    seen_odd = sorted({c - a for a, _, c in odd_first})
    seen_even = sorted({c - a for a, _, c in even_first})
    print()
    print(f"  charges realised with ODD  first leg (c <= {N}):  {seen_odd[:12]} ...")
    print(f"  charges realised with EVEN first leg (c <= {N}):  {seen_even[:12]} ...")
    print(f"  first twelve values of 2n^2                    :  "
          f"{[2*n*n for n in range(1, 13)]}")
    print(f"  first twelve odd squares                       :  "
          f"{[(2*m-1)**2 for m in range(1, 13)]}")
    print()
    print("  Realisability (every admissible charge occurs):")
    for n in range(1, 5):
        t = (2 * n + 1, 2 * n * n + 2 * n, 2 * n * n + 2 * n + 1)
        check(f"    (2n+1, 2n^2+2n, 2n^2+2n+1) with n={n} -> {t}, charge {t[2]-t[0]} = 2*{n}^2",
              qform(t) == 0 and gcd(t[0], t[1]) == 1 and t[2] - t[0] == 2 * n * n)
    for m in range(1, 5):
        t = (4 * m, 4 * m * m - 1, 4 * m * m + 1)
        check(f"    (4m, 4m^2-1, 4m^2+1) with m={m} -> {t}, charge {t[2]-t[0]} = ({2*m-1})^2",
              qform(t) == 0 and gcd(t[0], t[1]) == 1 and t[2] - t[0] == (2 * m - 1) ** 2)

    print("  Density-zero check: #{admissible charges <= X} grows like ~1.2 sqrt(X)")
    for X in (100, 1000, 10000, 100000):

        print(f"    X = {X:>7}:  count = {cnt:>5}   count/sqrt(X) = {cnt / X**0.5:.4f}")

from __future__ import annotations

from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Tuple

Triple = Tuple[int, int, int]
ROOT: Triple = (3, 4, 5)
E1: Triple = (1, 0, 1)

GENS: Dict[str, Callable[[Triple], Triple]] = {
    "A": lambda v: (v[0] - 2 * v[1] + 2 * v[2], 2 * v[0] - v[1] + 2 * v[2],
                    2 * v[0] - 2 * v[1] + 3 * v[2]),
    "B": lambda v: (v[0] + 2 * v[1] + 2 * v[2], 2 * v[0] + v[1] + 2 * v[2],
                    2 * v[0] + 2 * v[1] + 3 * v[2]),
    "C": lambda v: (-v[0] + 2 * v[1] + 2 * v[2], -2 * v[0] + v[1] + 2 * v[2],
                    -2 * v[0] + 2 * v[1] + 3 * v[2]),
}


def apply_word(word: str, v: Triple) -> Triple:
    for letter in word:
        v = GENS[letter](v)
    return v


def bil(v: Triple, w: Triple) -> int:
    return v[0] * w[0] + v[1] * w[1] - v[2] * w[2]


def chord_sq(v: Triple, p: Triple) -> Fraction:
    return ((Fraction(v[0], v[2]) - Fraction(p[0], p[2])) ** 2
            + (Fraction(v[1], v[2]) - Fraction(p[1], p[2])) ** 2)


def transported_spoke(word: str, n: int, length: int) -> List[Triple]:
    """The image under the isometry v -> W(A v) of the spoke of charge 2(n+1)^2 at (1,0).

    The spoke at (1,0) is the family C^j A^n root, j = 0, 1, 2, ...  Since
    A(1,0,1) = root, the map v -> W(A v) sends the boundary point (1,0) to the node
    W.root, and carries this spoke to a spoke of the same charge at that node.
    """
    base = apply_word("A" * n, ROOT)
    out: List[Triple] = []
    for _ in range(length):
        out.append(apply_word("A" + word, base))
        base = GENS["C"](base)
    return out


def report(word: str, spoke_indices: Tuple[int, ...] = (0, 1, 2, 3, 4)) -> None:
    p = apply_word(word, ROOT)
    px, py = Fraction(p[0], p[2]), Fraction(p[1], p[2])
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"star centre:  node with address {word!r}  =  {p}")
    print(f"plotted at    ({float(px):.9f}, {float(py):.9f})")
    print("=" * 78)
    for n in spoke_indices:
        d = 2 * (n + 1) ** 2
        fam = transported_spoke(word, n, 6)
        charges = {-bil(v, p) for v in fam}
        invs = {v[2] * chord_sq(v, p) for v in fam}
        assert charges == {d}, charges
        assert invs == {Fraction(2 * d, p[2])}, invs
        far = transported_spoke(word, n, 300)[-1]
        print(f"  spoke n={n+1:>2}  charge d = {d:>4}   "
              f"c*chord^2 = {invs.pop()!s:>10} = 2d/c_p   "
              f"far point dir = ({float(Fraction(far[0], far[2])):.9f}, "
              f"{float(Fraction(far[1], far[2])):.9f})")

    hyp: List[float] = []
    for _ in ks:

    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(outfile, dpi=165, facecolor=fig.get_facecolor())

    B: v => [ v[0]+2*v[1]+2*v[2],  2*v[0]+v[1]+2*v[2],  2*v[0]+2*v[1]+3*v[2]],

<div class="wrap">

  <p class="sub">
    The spokes of a star are labelled by the integer charge <em>d</em> = <em>c</em> − <em>a</em>.
    Not every integer is allowed. For a primitive triple the charge must be
    <b>twice a perfect square</b> (odd first leg) or an <b>odd perfect square</b> (even first
    leg) — a set of density zero. Sweep the number line below and watch the sieve.
  </p>

  <div class="card">
    <h2>1  ·  The admissible spectrum</h2>
    <label>Range  X = <span class="val" id="xLbl"></span></label>
    <input type="range" id="X" min="40" max="1200" step="10" value="300">
    <canvas id="sieve" width="1020" height="150"></canvas>
    <div class="key">
      <span><span class="sw" style="background:#ffd166"></span>2n² — charge of a triple with <b>odd</b> first leg (the Berggren tree)</span>
      <span><span class="sw" style="background:#5ad2ff"></span>odd n² — charge of a triple with <b>even</b> first leg</span>
      <span><span class="sw" style="background:#3a466e"></span>impossible</span>
    </div>
    <div class="out mono" id="stat"></div>
  </div>

  <div class="two">
    <div class="card">
      <h2>2  ·  Is d a legal charge?</h2>
      <label>Enter a positive integer d</label>
      <input type="text" id="dIn" value="18">
      <div class="out" id="dOut"></div>
    </div>

    <div class="card">
      <h2>3  ·  Descent: find a triple's address</h2>
      <label>Enter a, b, c (odd first leg, primitive)</label>
      <input type="text" id="tIn" value="119, 120, 169">
      <div class="out" id="tOut"></div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <h2>4  ·  How fast does the star fill in?</h2>
    <p class="sub" style="margin:0 0 10px">
      A node at depth <em>k</em> has spoke index <em>n</em> < 2·3<sup>k</sup>, always.
      The hyperbolic branch attains this up to the constant, with Pell indices
      2<sup>k</sup> ≤ n < 2·3<sup>k</sup>; the parabolic branch is the slowest
      possible, reaching index n only at depth n−1.

<script>
(function(){
  "use strict";
  const ROOT=[3,4,5];
  const G={A:v=>[v[0]-2*v[1]+2*v[2],2*v[0]-v[1]+2*v[2],2*v[0]-2*v[1]+3*v[2]],
           B:v=>[v[0]+2*v[1]+2*v[2],2*v[0]+v[1]+2*v[2],2*v[0]+2*v[1]+3*v[2]],
           C:v=>[-v[0]+2*v[1]+2*v[2],-2*v[0]+v[1]+2*v[2],-2*v[0]+2*v[1]+3*v[2]]};
  const IG={A:v=>[v[0]+2*v[1]-2*v[2],-2*v[0]-v[1]+2*v[2],-2*v[0]-2*v[1]+3*v[2]],
            B:v=>[v[0]+2*v[1]-2*v[2],2*v[0]+v[1]-2*v[2],-2*v[0]-2*v[1]+3*v[2]],
            C:v=>[-v[0]-2*v[1]+2*v[2],2*v[0]+v[1]-2*v[2],-2*v[0]-2*v[1]+3*v[2]]};
  const isq=n=>{let r=Math.round(Math.sqrt(n));while(r*r>n)r--;while((r+1)*(r+1)<=n)r++;return r;};
  const twiceSq = d => d%2===0 && isq(d/2)**2 === d/2;
  const oddSq   = d => { const r=isq(d); return r*r===d && r%2===1; };
  const gcd=(a,b)=>{a=Math.abs(a);b=Math.abs(b);while(b){[a,b]=[b,a%b];}return a;};

  // ---- 1. sieve ----
  const sv=document.getElementById("sieve"), sc=sv.getContext("2d");
  const Xs=document.getElementById("X");
  function sieve(){
    const X=parseInt(Xs.value,10);
    document.getElementById("xLbl").textContent=X;
    sc.clearRect(0,0,sv.width,sv.height);
    sc.fillStyle="#070b17"; sc.fillRect(0,0,sv.width,sv.height);
    const cols=Math.ceil(Math.sqrt(X*sv.width/sv.height));
    const cell=Math.min(sv.width/cols, 26);
    const perRow=Math.floor(sv.width/cell);
    let e=0,o=0;
    for(let d=1;d<=X;d++){
      const i=d-1, cx=(i%perRow)*cell, cy=Math.floor(i/perRow)*cell;
      let col="#3a466e";
      if(twiceSq(d)){col="#ffd166";e++;} else if(oddSq(d)){col="#5ad2ff";o++;}
      sc.fillStyle=col;
      sc.fillRect(cx+1,cy+1,Math.max(1,cell-2),Math.max(1,cell-2));
    }
    const tot=e+o;
    document.getElementById("stat").innerHTML =
      "admissible charges d \u2264 " + X + ":  <span class='val'>" + tot + "</span>" +
      "  (" + e + " of the form 2n\u00B2, " + o + " odd squares)<br>" +
      "density  " + (tot/X*100).toFixed(2) + "%  —  " +
      "count / \u221AX = " + (tot/Math.sqrt(X)).toFixed(3) +
      "  <span style='color:#93a0c4'>(so the spectrum has density zero: the star is sparse)</span>";
  }
  Xs.addEventListener("input",sieve); sieve();

  // ---- 2. legality test ----
  const dIn=document.getElementById("dIn"), dOut=document.getElementById("dOut");
  function testD(){
    const d=parseInt(dIn.value.trim(),10);
    if(!(d>0)){dOut.innerHTML="<span class='no'>enter a positive integer</span>";return;}
    if(twiceSq(d)){
      const n=isq(d/2);
      const t=[2*n+1, 2*n*n+2*n, 2*n*n+2*n+1];
      dOut.innerHTML="<span class='big'>d = "+d+" = 2\u00B7"+n+"\u00B2</span><br>"+
        "<span class='ok'>✓ legal</span> — charge of a triple with <b>odd</b> first leg, "+
        "so it is a spoke of the star drawn by the tree.<br>"+
        "<span class='mono'>witness (2n+1, 2n\u00B2+2n, 2n\u00B2+2n+1) = ("+t.join(", ")+")"+
        "   c\u2212a = "+(t[2]-t[0])+"</span><br>"+
        "<span class='mono'>spoke index n = "+n+"</span>";
    } else if(oddSq(d)){
      const n=isq(d), m=(n+1)/2;
      const t=[4*m, 4*m*m-1, 4*m*m+1];
      dOut.innerHTML="<span class='big'>d = "+d+" = "+n+"\u00B2 (n odd)</span><br>"+
        "<span class='ok'>✓ legal</span> — charge of a triple with <b>even</b> first leg; "+
        "such triples are the tree nodes with the legs swapped.<br>"+
        "<span class='mono'>witness (4m, 4m\u00B2\u22121, 4m\u00B2+1) = ("+t.join(", ")+")"+
        "   c\u2212a = "+(t[2]-t[0])+"</span>";
    } else {
      dOut.innerHTML="<span class='big'>d = "+d+"</span><br>"+
        "<span class='no'>× impossible</span> — no primitive Pythagorean triple has "+
        "this charge, so no spoke of any star carries this label.";
    }
  }
  dIn.addEventListener("input",testD); testD();

  // ---- 3. descent ----
  const tIn=document.getElementById("tIn"), tOut=document.getElementById("tOut");
  function descend(){
    const parts=tIn.value.split(/[ ,;]+/).filter(s=>s.length).map(Number);
    if(parts.length!==3 || parts.some(x=>!Number.isInteger(x)||x<=0)){
      tOut.innerHTML="<span class='no'>enter three positive integers</span>";return;}
    let [a,b,c]=parts;
    if(a*a+b*b!==c*c){tOut.innerHTML="<span class='no'>not a Pythagorean triple</span>";return;}
    if(gcd(a,b)!==1){tOut.innerHTML="<span class='no'>not primitive</span>";return;}
    if(a%2===0){tOut.innerHTML="<span class='no'>first leg must be odd (swap the legs)</span>";return;}
    let v=[a,b,c], word=[], guard=0;
    while(!(v[0]===3&&v[1]===4&&v[2]===5) && guard++<200){
      let moved=false;
      for(const g of ["A","B","C"]){
        const w=IG[g](v);
        if(w[0]>0&&w[1]>0&&w[2]>0&&w[2]<v[2]&&w[0]*w[0]+w[1]*w[1]===w[2]*w[2]){
          word.push(g); v=w; moved=true; break;
        }
      }
      if(!moved) break;
    }
    if(!(v[0]===3&&v[1]===4&&v[2]===5)){
      tOut.innerHTML="<span class='no'>descent failed (numeric overflow?)</span>";return;}
    const addr=word.reverse().join("");
    let u=ROOT; for(const g of addr) u=G[g](u);
    const m=isq((c+a)/2), n=isq((c-a)/2);
    const nB=(addr.match(/B/g)||[]).length;
    tOut.innerHTML=
      "<span class='big'>"+(addr===""?"\u03B5":addr)+"</span>  <span class='mono'>(depth "+addr.length+")</span><br>"+
      "<span class='mono'>replay from (3,4,5): ("+u.join(", ")+")"+
      (u[0]===a&&u[1]===b&&u[2]===c?" <span class='ok'>✓</span>":" <span class='no'>×</span>")+"</span><br>"+
      "<span class='mono'>Euclid (m,n) = ("+m+", "+n+")   spoke index "+Math.min(m,n)+
      "   charge "+(c-a)+" = 2\u00B7"+n+"\u00B2</span><br>"+
      "<span class='mono'>Lyapunov: 5\u00B73^"+nB+" = "+(5*Math.pow(3,nB))+
      " \u2264 "+c+" \u2264 5\u00B77^"+addr.length+" = "+(5*Math.pow(7,addr.length))+
      " <span class='ok'>✓</span></span>";
  }
  tIn.addEventListener("input",descend); descend();

  // ---- 4. growth table ----
  (function(){
    let rows="<tr><th>depth k</th><th>2<sup>k</sup></th><th>Pell index (branch B)</th>"+
             "<th>index (branch A)</th><th>index (branch C)</th><th>2·3<sup>k</sup></th></tr>";
    let pell=[1,2]; while(pell.length<11) pell.push(2*pell[pell.length-1]+pell[pell.length-2]);
    for(let k=0;k<10;k++){
      rows+="<tr><td>"+k+"</td><td>"+Math.pow(2,k)+"</td>"+
            "<td style='color:#ffd166'>"+pell[k]+"</td>"+
            "<td style='color:#8affc1'>"+(k+1)+"</td>"+
            "<td style='color:#5ad2ff'>1</td>"+
            "<td>"+(2*Math.pow(3,k))+"</td></tr>";
    }
    document.getElementById("growth").innerHTML=rows;
  })();
})();
</script>
</body>
</html>
"
    }

  "interactive_layout": "# Stars on the Rim
### A guided tour of the boundary geometry of the Pythagorean tree

---

## 0. A picture that shouldn't have been there

Every right triangle with whole-number sides — $3,4,5$; $5,12,13$; $8,15,17$ — solves
$$a^2+b^2=c^2.$$
In 1963 F. J. M. Barning discovered (and A. Hall rediscovered in 1970, after B. Berggren
in 1934) that **every** primitive such triple is reachable from $(3,4,5)$ by three integer
matrices, each triple exactly once. The solutions of the oldest equation in mathematics
form a perfect infinite ternary tree.

Trees of large integers are hard to look at. So let us draw the tree differently. Send
each triple to the direction
$$\mathrm{dir}(a,b,c) = \left(\tfrac ac,\ \tfrac bc\right),$$
a point of the unit circle, and place it at a radius that creeps towards $1$ as the
hypotenuse grows. Join each node to its three children.

What comes out is not a spray of dots. It is full of structure — and the strangest part is
that curves seem to gather into **bundles converging on isolated points of the boundary
circle itself**, like light sources embedded in the rim.

Play with it before reading anything else. Change the star centre. Watch the colours
reorganise.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

> **What just happened.** The colours are not decoration. Each colour is a single value of
> an integer invariant — the *charge* — and each set of same-coloured nodes lies on a
> single curve running into the star centre. The rest of this page explains why that
> integer exists and why it controls the entire picture.

---

## 1. Right triangles are points on a light cone

Rewrite the Pythagorean equation as
$$Q(a,b,c) := a^2+b^2-c^2 = 0.$$
$Q$ has signature $(2,1)$ — the signature of two-dimensional spacetime. Its zero set is a
**light cone**, and Pythagorean triples are exactly the integer points on it. Polarize it:
$$\langle v, w\rangle = v_1w_1 + v_2w_2 - v_3w_3.$$

Now the decisive computation. The three Berggren generators are
$$
\begin{aligned}
A(a,b,c) &= (\,a-2b+2c,\ 2a-b+2c,\ 2a-2b+3c\,),\\
B(a,b,c) &= (\,a+2b+2c,\ 2a+b+2c,\ 2a+2b+3c\,),\\
C(a,b,c) &= (-a+2b+2c,\ -2a+b+2c,\ -2a+2b+3c\,),
\end{aligned}
$$
and every one of them satisfies $\langle Mv, Mw\rangle = \langle v,w\rangle$ exactly.

<details>
<summary><b>Show me the check</b></summary>

For $C$, expand $\langle Cv, Cw\rangle$ with $v=(a,b,c)$, $w=(x,y,z)$:
$$(-a+2b+2c)(-x+2y+2z) + (-2a+b+2c)(-2x+y+2z) - (-2a+2b+3c)(-2x+2y+3z).$$
Collecting the nine bilinear monomials, the coefficients of $ay$, $az$, $bx$, $bz$, $cx$,
$cy$ all cancel, and what survives is $ax+by-cz = \langle v,w\rangle$. The same happens for
$A$ and $B$. There is nothing clever here — it is the statement that these three integer
matrices lie in the orthogonal group $O(2,1;\mathbb{Z})$, which is a fact one simply
verifies.
</details>

$O(2,1;\mathbb{Z})$ is the isometry group of the hyperbolic plane in the hyperboloid
(Klein) model, and $\mathrm{dir}$ is the map sending a null ray to its **ideal point** — a
point on the circle at infinity. **The plot is not a picture of arithmetic. It is a picture
of a discrete group acting on hyperbolic space.**

---

## 2. One identity, from which everything follows

Here is the whole theory in one line. For two Pythagorean triples $v$ and $p$ with
positive hypotenuses $c_v$, $c_p$:

$$\boxed{\ \bigl\|\mathrm{dir}\,v - \mathrm{dir}\,p\bigr\|^2 \;=\; \frac{-2\langle v,p\rangle}{c_v\,c_p}\ }$$

The left side is *visual* — the squared straight-line distance between two dots you drew.
The right side is *arithmetic*. Define the **charge** of $v$ at $p$ to be the positive
integer $d = -\langle v,p\rangle$.

<details>
<summary><b>Show me the two-line proof</b></summary>

With $v=(a,b,c)$, $p=(x,y,z)$,
$$\Bigl(\tfrac ac-\tfrac xz\Bigr)^2+\Bigl(\tfrac bc-\tfrac yz\Bigr)^2
=\frac{a^2+b^2}{c^2}+\frac{x^2+y^2}{z^2}-\frac{2(ax+by)}{cz}
= 1+1-\frac{2(ax+by)}{cz},$$
using $a^2+b^2=c^2$ and $x^2+y^2=z^2$. Since $\langle v,p\rangle = ax+by-cz$, this is
$2-2\bigl(\langle v,p\rangle+cz\bigr)/(cz) = -2\langle v,p\rangle/(cz)$. $\blacksquare$
</details>

Read the identity again. If a whole family of triples shares the **same** charge at a fixed
$p$, and their hypotenuses run to infinity, the numerator is frozen while the denominator
explodes. The distance to $\mathrm{dir}\,p$ collapses.

> **Star Theorem.** Let $p$ be a Pythagorean triple and let $v_1, v_2, \dots$ be
> Pythagorean triples with $\langle v_k, p\rangle = -d$ for all $k$ and hypotenuse tending
> to infinity. Then the plotted points $\mathrm{dir}\,v_k$ converge to $\mathrm{dir}\,p$.

One curve per value of $d$; all of them running into one boundary point. **That is the
star.** In hyperbolic language the level set $\{\langle v,p\rangle=-d\}$ is a **horocycle**
based at $\mathrm{dir}\,p$ — a circle internally tangent to the boundary.

---

## 3. Exactly how the curves touch the rim

Multiply the boxed identity by $c_v$:

$$c_v \cdot \bigl\|\mathrm{dir}\,v - \mathrm{dir}\,p\bigr\|^2 \;=\; \frac{2d}{c_p}.$$

This is not an asymptotic statement. Along a horocycle the left side is **exactly
constant**, with no error term. Two consequences pin down the shape:

- $c_v^2 \cdot \|\mathrm{dir}\,v - \mathrm{dir}\,p\|^2 \to \infty$;
- $\sqrt{c_v} \cdot \|\mathrm{dir}\,v - \mathrm{dir}\,p\|^2 \to 0$.

The contact order with the boundary circle is **exactly two**. A geodesic through the
centre of the disc — a straight radius — has contact order one. That single unit of
difference is what your eye registers as "these ones are bending".

The middle panel below shows the invariant staying rigidly flat along four different
spokes while it wanders along a geodesic. The right panel shows the contact order directly.

{{visualization:1}}

<details>
<summary><b>Why is contact order two the "horocyclic" order?</b></summary>

A horocycle in the Klein disc is a Euclidean circle internally tangent to the boundary. If
it has Euclidean radius $\rho$ and touches at $P$, a point of it at distance $\varepsilon$
from the rim is at angular offset $\approx\sqrt{2\rho\varepsilon}$ from $P$ — squared
offset proportional to $\varepsilon$. Since we draw a node of hypotenuse $c$ at radius
$1-1/c$, the radial defect is $\varepsilon = 1/c$, and squared offset proportional to
$1/c$ is precisely the boxed identity. So the picture drawn on the screen satisfies the
exact algebraic law
$$\bigl\|\mathrm{dir}\,v - \mathrm{dir}\,p\bigr\|^2 = \frac{2d\,(1-r)}{c_p},\qquad r=1-\tfrac1c,$$
with $d/c_p$ the only parameter. That is the shape you are looking at.
</details>

---

## 4. Two kinds of motion: why some things curve and others streak

The three generators behave differently because they have different *conjugacy types* as
hyperbolic isometries — and conjugacy type is exactly what the eye is picking up.

| generator | type | conserves | iterates | limit point | rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $C$ | parabolic | $c-a$ | quadratic in $k$ | $(1,0)$, rational | $\Theta(k^{-2})$ |
| $A$ | parabolic | $c-b$ | quadratic in $k$ | $(0,1)$, rational | $\Theta(k^{-2})$ |
| $B$ | hyperbolic | $\lvert a-b\rvert$ | exponential in $k$ | angle $\pi/4$, **irrational** | $O(3^{-k})$ |

<details>
<summary><b>The exact closed forms (this is where "parabolic" comes from)</b></summary>

With $d=c-a$ and $e=c-b$,
$$C^k(a,b,c) = \bigl(\gamma_k - d,\ b+2kd,\ \gamma_k\bigr), \qquad \gamma_k = c+2kb+2k^2d,$$
$$A^k(a,b,c) = \bigl(a+2ke,\ \alpha_k-e,\ \alpha_k\bigr), \qquad \alpha_k = c+2ka+2k^2e.$$
The hypotenuse is a genuine **quadratic polynomial** in the step number, which is the
fingerprint of a rank-three unipotent Jordan block: these are parabolic isometries, and
their orbits crawl along horocycles.

By contrast, $B$ satisfies the Pell recursion on hypotenuses,
$$c_{k+2} = 6c_{k+1}-c_k,$$
whose characteristic roots are the units $3\pm2\sqrt2 = (1\pm\sqrt2)^2$ of
$\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt2]$. Each step multiplies the hypotenuse by at least $5$. An orbit of $B$
slides along a **geodesic**.
</details>

Starting from the root $(3,4,5)$, the rates are explicit for every $k\ge1$:
$$\frac{2}{17k^2} \;\le\; 1 - x\bigl(C^k(3,4,5)\bigr), \qquad\qquad \Bigl| x\bigl(B^k(3,4,5)\bigr) - \tfrac{\sqrt2}{2} \Bigr| \;\le\; \frac{1}{5\cdot 3^{k}}.$$

The left panel of the figure above shows both, against their bounds.

And here is a punchline you can see in the disc widget by switching on the $\pi/4$ marker:
the hyperbolic limit sits at $x=\sqrt2/2$, which is **irrational**, while every plotted
point has rational coordinates. So at $\pi/4$ there is no star — just one lonely geodesic
arriving, with nothing waiting for it.

> **Stars can occur only at rational ideal points.**

---

## 5. Which stars are allowed: quantization

Now the arithmetic comes back, and it is sharp. At the point $(1,0)$ the charge is
$d = c-a$. Which integers can occur?

> **Charge Quantization Theorem.** If $a^2+b^2=c^2$ with $a,b,c>0$ and $\gcd(a,b)=1$, then
> $c-a$ is **twice a perfect square** (when $a$ is odd) or an **odd perfect square** (when
> $a$ is even). Conversely every such value occurs: $(2n+1,\,2n^2+2n,\,2n^2+2n+1)$ realises
> $c-a=2n^2$, and $(4m,\,4m^2-1,\,4m^2+1)$ realises $c-a=(2m-1)^2$.

<details>
<summary><b>Show me the proof (odd first leg)</b></summary>

Both legs cannot be odd, since then $a^2+b^2\equiv2\pmod4$ and no square is. So $b=2b'$ is
even, and $c$ is odd. Write $c-a=2u$, $c+a=2v$. From $b^2=(c-a)(c+a)$ we get $uv=b'^2$.
Primitivity gives $\gcd(a,c)=1$ (because $a$ is coprime to $b^2=c^2-a^2$, hence to $c$),
and since $c=u+v$, $a=v-u$, a Bézout combination shows $\gcd(u,v)=1$. Two coprime positive
integers whose product is a square are each a square; so $u=n^2$ and $c-a=2n^2$.
$\blacksquare$
</details>

So the spokes are labelled by
$$\{2, 8, 18, 32, 50,\dots\}\ \cup\ \{1,9,25,49,\dots\},$$
a set of **density zero**. Inside the tree — where every node has odd first leg — the
spectrum shrinks to exactly $\{2n^2: n\ge1\}$, and nothing else ever occurs.

*This is why the star is a star and not a smear.* Sweep the sieve below and watch the
density collapse; then feed the tool an integer and see whether it can be a spoke label.
